newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee steady in spot, forward premiums rise.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee steady in spot, forward premiums rise.

text.p: The Indian rupee was steady against the dollar in late Monday morning spot deals but was weak in the forward market, dealers said.
They said the spot rupee was traded between 35.7275 and 35.7300 per dollar. Spot rupee opened at 35.72/73.
"There is genuine corporate demand," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "It is all from Bombay-based banks."
"I have done September (dollars) at 16.5/17.0 paise," said the chief dealer at a leading brokerage. September dollars ended Thursday, the last working day, at 13/15 paise.
"We think it is a good strategy to cover near term liabilities," said an executive at a manufacturing firm.
"Premiums are also up in far forward maturities," said a bank dealer.
Dealers attributed the rise to rising trend in the overnight call money market. Call money was quoted at 8.5-9.0 percent in latest deals.
"There is also some talk that the overvalued rupee may come under pressure in the long run," said a dealer.
